# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-13 (Extended v108)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 4)**: (1) Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon; le Petit-Picpus convent district; M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens (Rue de l'Ouest side); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Staveford, Gulhaven). **Environmental conditions (Spring Year 4)**: warm air, light and shadow in Luxembourg, sky pure, sparrows chirping in chestnut-trees; rain threatening since morning but holding off; frost silvering hedges overnight; bell for vespers rings thinly; baker's boy late, line at oven grows long; children chasing hoop shrieking down lane.

## Primary Locations
**LUXEMBOURG GARDENS**: Fountain basin with swans; statues; "his alley" on Rue de l'Ouest side with recurring bench where mysterious couple observed—specific bench surrounded by aureole in narrative focus. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus convent. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet, 30 francs annually. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz; thatched cottage, fifty crowns yearly.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as assistant gardener in convent; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. Nuns unaware of circumstances.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. **Status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps around Gorbeau house; confident convict nearby.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development Continued

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, now twenty years old (as of current spring Year 4); three years since left grandfather.

**Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen; believes grandfather burned it.

**Political evolution (Winter Year 3 → Spring Year 4)**: Converted to Bonapartism and republicanism; political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 calmed views. No longer held firm opinions; sympathies directed to humanity over nation, woman over people, idea over deed, poet over hero. Preferred introspection to action.

**Material condition (Spring Year 4)**: Occupied Gorbeau cabinet 30 francs annually. Daily sustenance cost 20 sous (365 francs yearly); clothing 100 francs; linen/washing 100 francs. Total: 450 francs. No fireplace. Wardrobe: two black suits, three shirts. Earned approximately seven hundred francs yearly from law practice and publisher M. Magimel's work (prospectuses, translation, annotation, biography compilation). **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered lodging, regular occupation, fifteen hundred francs yearly—Marius refused to preserve liberty and dignity.

**Philosophy (Winter Year 3)**: After securing living with certainty, deliberately stopped working to dedicate time to thought and meditation. Spent entire days dreaming. Real character revealed through aspirations and dreams more surely than deliberate ideas. Each dreams according to his nature.

**Pleasures and habits (Winter Year 3)**: Long solitary walks on outer boulevards, Champs-de-Mars, Luxembourg's least frequented alleys. Spent half-days observing market gardens. Attended occasional evening parties at generals' homes in freezing weather (could not afford carriage); wore new coat.

**Previous attitude toward women (Winter Year 3)**: At period of abject misery, believed young girls stared mockingly at his old clothes; actually they stared because of his grace and dreamed of him. Did not flee from: bearded old woman chambermaid (Courfeyrac jested); little girl he saw often and never looked at.

**Grandfather quarrel**: Violent quarrel three years ago; remained estranged without rapprochement—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C**: Met Courfeyrac at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends. Courfeyrac introduced him to Café Musain. Did not enter decidedly into group presided by Enjolras but remained cordial. Close to **M. Mabeuf**—owed him revolution within soul; indebted for knowing and loving his father.

## The Mysterious Couple at Luxembourg: Development (Current Focus)

**Initial six-month observation (over one year prior)**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty years old and very young girl (thirteen/fourteen) seated daily on bench, Rue de l'Ouest side. Man: retired military officer, robust, weary, kindly but unapproachable; wore blue trousers, blue frock coat, broad-brimmed hat (always new), black cravat, white quaker shirt, white hair. Girl: thin, almost homely, awkward, insignificant, with promise of handsome eyes; wore badly cut black merino gown (convent scholar dress). Appeared father and daughter. Conversed peacefully; girl chattered, man fixed eyes on her with ineffable paternity.

**Six-month interruption**: Observation ceased for unknown reason.

**Reunion and girl's transformation (Summer Year 3)**: Marius returned to Luxembourg on serene morning. At first thought she was another daughter; on second examination recognized her as same girl. **In six months little girl had become young maiden—rare phenomenon when girls blossom suddenly.** No longer school-girl in felt hat and scholar shoes; became well-dressed person. Wore dress of black damask, cape of same material, bonnet of white crape, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe. Whole toilette exhaled youthful penetrating perfume.

**Marius's indifference (Summer Year 3)**: When she raised eyelids, Marius approached but found in her veiled azure only child's glance. She looked at him indifferently as at brat or marble vase. Marius continued promenade, thought about something else. Paid no further attention; passed near bench habitually; thought no more about girl now beautiful than when homely.

**First meaningful glance (Spring Year 4—Chapter 13 opening)**: On warm day, Luxembourg inundated with light and shade, pure sky, sparrows twittering in chestnut-trees. Marius threw open his whole soul to nature, not thinking of anything, simply living and breathing. As he passed near the bench, the young girl raised her eyes to him. **Their glances met.**

Narrative reflection: That first gaze of a soul which does not yet know itself is like dawn in sky—awakening of something radiant and strange. Dangerous charm of unexpected gleam composed of all innocence of present and all passion of future. Undecided tenderness revealing itself by chance. Virgin maiden sets snare unknown to herself, capturing hearts without wishing or knowing. Virgin looking like woman.

**Marius's awakening (Spring Year 4)**: That evening returning to garret, Marius perceived for first time he had gone to Luxembourg in everyday clothes: battered hat, coarse carter's boots, black trousers white at knees, black coat pale at elbows. Resolved to dress differently. On subsequent day to Luxembourg, made tour of fountain basin, contemplated statues and bourgeois scolding child about excess. Directed course to "his alley" slowly, as if forced to go yet withheld—did not perceive contradiction himself. Buttoned coat to top, pulled down to eliminate wrinkles, examined trousers with complaisance. Marched on bench like Hannibal on Rome—yet movements purely mechanical; mind occupied with _Manuel du Baccalauréat_, tragedies of Racine, comedies of Molière. Piercing whistling in ears.

**Approach and retreat (Spring Year 4)**: As he drew near, pace slackened. At some distance from bench, before reaching walk's end, he halted and retraced steps. Could not explain himself. Did not attempt to approach bench again; halted near middle of walk—unprecedented. For first time in fifteen months, reflected that gentleman who sat there daily with daughter had likely noticed his assiduity and considered it singular. Held himself erect in case observed from behind. Rose after quarter hour as though resuming march toward aureole-surrounded bench, but remained standing motionless.

**New costume ritual (Spring Year 4)**: Following day, Ma'am Burgon (housekeeper, styled "Ma'am Bougon" by Courfeyrac) observed with stupefaction that M. Marius wore his new coat again. Returned to Luxembourg, seated himself midway on bench, surveying white bonnet, black dress, blue light from distance. Did not stir; only left when gates closed. Concluded they departed by Rue de l'Ouest gate. Never recalled where he dined that evening.

**Fortnight of vigil (Spring Year 4)**: Marius went to Luxembourg no longer to stroll but to seat himself always in same spot without knowing why. Put on new coat every morning for purpose of not showing himself, began anew next day. Young girl was decidedly marvelous beauty. Only criticism: contradiction between melancholy gaze and merry smile gave wild effect, sometimes made sweet countenance strange without ceasing to be charming.

## M. Mabeuf

**Character**: Ecclesiastic, botanist, editor, man of books and flowers.

**Servant—Mother Plutarque (Spring Year 4)**: Innocent spinster; cat Sultan filled her heart; glory consisted in white caps; could read. Mother Plutarque fell asleep in chair before fire caught.

**New residence (Winter Year 3)**: Relocated to village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; established in thatched cottage for fifty crowns yearly with three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge with well. Carried _Flora_, copper-plates, herbariums, portfolios, books. On entrance night, perceived Mother Plutarque's melancholy; tapped her shoulder: "We have the indigo!"

**Philosophical disposition**: Brain absorbed in wisdom or folly slowly; results in passivity resembling philosophy. Habits swung like pendulum; once mounted on illusion, remained long after illusion disappeared. Recently enjoyed Mother Plutarque reading aloud "Bouddha and the Dragon"; M. Mabeuf interjected about dragon, called it good book, most beautiful legend.

## Friends of the A B C (Revolutionary Organization)

**Identity and purpose**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—_Abaissé_, the debased (the people). Wished to elevate people. Secret society in embryonic state, not numerous.

**Meetings (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Back room Café Musain; argand lamp lighted. Nearly all haranguing; tossed words, caught up in turn. Peaceable tumults.

**Members**: Enjolras (believer, sober), Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students; cordial with working classes.

## English Provincial Towns

**Population movements**: Yera Haskick (Dunstead → Kelmere); Rinelle (Kelford → Torton); Kadrek Brackick (followed to Torton). **Births**: Ferald and Isvie Stenworth (son/daughter, Dunstead, parents Luwyn Brackick); Zavus Prydenridge (son, Ostcombe, parents Wenelle and Rovus).

**Activities and observations (Winter/Spring Year 4)**: Isric Thornmere mended torn sleeve by window, spoke little; asked Wenelle "Will it rain?"—she shrugged. Rozek Stenenridge told Luena "You look tired"; Luena did not deny. Yera Haskick laughed alone at story; told Gadan Corrley (tired) Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood. Vesmira Thornmere and Wenelle Lindmere discussed weather, harvest, lame horse. Taric Corrley complained aching back as usual. Taric walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Kadan bought ribbon then regretted. Lurald Stenworth argued with carter over sack of oats price. Peten Haskick said "salt price a scandal"—Ulrald agreed. Kassa Brackick confided to Yewyn Corrford mill ledger rewritten. Ferald Stenworth fell asleep before fire caught. Ulrald Corrford counted coins twice, came up penny short. Yewyn Corrford fell asleep before fire caught. Rorald Lindmere gave Gadan Corrley solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Ravenmere.

**Claims and rumors (prior)**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (claim). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body). Granary fire set on purpose (rumor). Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten. Taric Corrley previously agreed salt price scandal with Pelia Lindmere.

## Winter Year 3 Events (Paris)

**Student assembly**: Students of law and medicine summoned to Place du Panthéon at midday to deliberate on artillery of National Guard—conflict between Minister of War and citizen's militia over cannon at Louvre courtyard.

**M. Gillenormand's rage**: Read announcement in Royalist sheet; flew into rage; denounced students as pack of brats, Republicans as one nose and handkerchief with galley-slaves. Called progress madness, humanity dream, revolution crime, republic monster.

**New scheming (Winter Year 3)**: Aunt Gillenormand plotted to have Lieutenant Théodule (nephew, lancer regiment) take Marius's place. Théodule entered in plain clothes as bourgeois, discreetly introduced. M. Gillenormand, after painful reverie before entrance, thought no more of grandnephew after reading.
